description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and accuracy (ACC, %) (y-axis) for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” spans from 0 to approximately 10⁴ on a logarithmic scale, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, ranges from 60% to 85% with major tick marks at 60, 65, 70, 75, 80, and 85. Each method is represented by a distinct line with a unique color and marker: Base (black circles, solid line), FT (blue downward triangles, solid line), IKE (red upward triangles, solid line), MEND (brown diamonds, solid line), MEMIT (purple pentagons, solid line), and ROME (green squares, solid line). All lines show a general upward trend as co-occurrence number increases. At the lowest co-occurrence (near 1), Base starts at ~64%, FT at ~65.5%, IKE at ~67.5%, MEND at ~71%, MEMIT at ~70%, and ROME at ~74.5%. At the highest co-occurrence (~10⁴), Base reaches ~71%, FT ~73%, IKE ~75.5%, MEND ~80.5%, MEMIT ~77.5%, and ROME ~83%. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence levels, while Base remains the lowest. The gap between ROME and the other methods widens as co-occurrence increases.
